availability_evidence: Annual report pages 55 and 90 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 17 December 2019; corporate-successor-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Continuing revenue rose 34% to £28.3m and adjusted operating profit more than doubled to £2.2m, while leverage improved from 2.3x to 1.8x and all facility covenants were met. Gross margin nevertheless fell from 34.2% to 32.4%, total net debt rose from £6.7m to £11.4m, cash conversion was below target and the auditor identified a material going-concern uncertainty linked to a contingent liability.
already_announced_exclusion: The Alternative Energy and Hydratron disposals, PMC restructuring, management changes, refinancing and other operational changes disclosed or completed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Strong revenue and adjusted-profit recovery and lower leverage provide substantial offsets, but rising debt, weak conversion and an explicit material going-concern uncertainty create material cash and intervention pressure.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 65 and 96 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 17 January 2022; identical corporate-successor-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue was flat at £25.3m and adjusted operating loss narrowed from £2.4m to £0.7m, while gross margin improved from 21.1% to 26.6% and net debt fell from £7.4m to £4.9m. However, PMC revenue fell 55% and its return on revenue was negative 26%; operations used £6.6m cash versus a £1.7m inflow, the bank facility required amendment with temporary liquidity and capex covenants, and the Group remained loss-making amid prolonged market disruption.
already_announced_exclusion: The Quadscot closure, February 2021 PMC reorganisation, redundancies, equity fundraising, Greenlane note repayment, refinancing and other Covid-response actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A severe operating cash reversal, continuing Group loss, deep PMC contraction and covenant amendment create high intervention pressure. Margin recovery, reduced losses and lower reported debt are meaningful but depended partly on equity and disposal-related receipts.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 47 and 87 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 29 January 2024; identical corporate-successor-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 28% to £32.0m, gross margin from 21% to 28%, adjusted EBITDA from a £0.9m loss to a £2.1m profit and adjusted operating result from a £2.6m loss to a £0.6m profit. Orders rose 75%, both divisions returned to positive EBITDA and net debt fell to £2.4m. Cash before financing still declined £0.5m, liquidity depended partly on an equity raise and shareholder term loan, and CSC faced an expected near-term revenue transition; no material going-concern uncertainty was identified.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced PMC divestment, £2.1m equity raise, November 2023 shareholder term loan and warrants, senior-management reorganisation and operational-improvement programme disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The operating turnaround, margin expansion, record orders and reduced debt dominate the evidence. Residual cash dependence, refinancing and the expected CSC transition create contained pressure, while the already-announced PMC divestment cannot count prospectively.
